response:
I have identified and resolved the proxy authentication issue.

### Root Cause
When proxy URLs containing authentication credentials (e.g. `http://user:pass@proxy.com:8080`) were processed by [`prepend_scheme_if_needed`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-_tqfmggb/requests/utils.py#L960), the function reconstructed the URL using `parsed.netloc` from `urllib3.util.parse_url`. In `urllib3`, `parsed.netloc` returns only `host:port` and does not include `auth` credentials. Consequently, `urlunparse` stripped `user:pass@` from the proxy URL, preventing [`get_auth_from_url`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-_tqfmggb/requests/utils.py#L985) from extracting credentials and leading to missing `Proxy-Authorization` headers (resulting in HTTP 407 status codes). Additionally, [`get_auth_from_url`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-_tqfmggb/requests/utils.py#L985) failed when `parsed.password` was `None`, and [`rebuild_proxies`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-_tqfmggb/requests/sessions.py#L272) only looked up direct scheme keys rather than using [`select_proxy`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-_tqfmggb/requests/utils.py#L811).

### Fix
1. In [`prepend_scheme_if_needed`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-_tqfmggb/requests/utils.py#L960), preserve `auth` when present by combining `f'{auth}@{netloc}'` prior to calling `urlunparse`.
2. In [`get_auth_from_url`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-_tqfmggb/requests/utils.py#L985), safely unquote `parsed.username` and `parsed.password` even when either component is `None`.
3. In [`rebuild_proxies`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-_tqfmggb/requests/sessions.py#L272), use [`select_proxy`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-_tqfmggb/requests/utils.py#L811) to resolve proxy configuration across all key types (e.g. `'all'`, `'https'`).
